hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: A horizontal line can intersect line chart segments at integer heights or halfway between integers.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Double all coordinates by multiplying each y-value by 2 to map all half-integer coordinates to integers.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Represent each line segment as a vertical interval [min(start, end), max(start, end)] and use a difference event map to count overlapping intervals.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxIntersectionCount(self, y: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(y)
        events = defaultdict(int)
        for i in range(1, n):
            start = 2 * y[i - 1]
            end = 2 * y[i]
            if i < n - 1:
                if y[i] > y[i - 1]:
                    end -= 1
                else:
                    end += 1
            events[min(start, end)] += 1
            events[max(start, end) + 1] -= 1
        curr = 0
        ans = 0
        for k in sorted(events.keys()):
            curr += events[k]
            ans = max(ans, curr)
        return ans
```

variables: n: number of vertices in line chart
complexity.notes: Coordinate doubling followed by sorting sweep-line event points.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every possible continuous height takes unbounded or quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary hash table for sweep-line difference array events.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use coordinate doubling to turn half-integer level sets into discrete integer events without float precision loss.

solutions.approach: Coordinate Doubling with Sweep-Line Difference Map
